article.articleHeadline: Influenza A in Brazil: Vaccination efforts intensify amid rising infection rates
article.articleSummary: As of March 21, 2026, Brazil is experiencing a significant increase in Influenza A activity, with Severe Acute Respiratory Infection (SARI) cases rising by 17%, totaling 1,135 in Ceará alone. Influenza A is responsible for 28.6% of SARI-related deaths this year, contributing to a total of 865 deaths from Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome (SRAG). In response, the health ministry has launched three national vaccination campaigns from March 28 to May 30, targeting priority groups to enhance immunization coverage. The autumn-winter peak is approaching, with 20,300 SARI cases reported by March 20, 2026. Regional increases are noted in states like Mato Grosso, Rio de Janeiro, and Espírito Santo, emphasizing the urgent need for vaccination. In Acre, vaccination coverage remains critically low, with only 7.79% of children and 13.72% of pregnant women vaccinated. Despite a slight uptick in SRAG hospitalizations driven by RSV, Rhinovirus, and Influenza A, deaths have decreased to 16 in 2026, down from previous years.

article.articleHeadline: Rabies in Vietnam: Urgent measures following recent dog bite incidents
article.articleSummary: In March 2026, Đắk Lắk Province experienced a rabies outbreak after a rabid dog bit six individuals, prompting immediate health interventions. The local health department implemented urgent rabies prevention measures, including enhanced pet vaccination and area delimitation. In 2025, the region reported seven rabies-related deaths, highlighting the ongoing threat. Following the recent incidents, local authorities culled 11 neighboring dogs and quarantined over 200 animals to prevent further transmission. The victims received timely vaccinations and are currently stable, with no symptoms reported. The provincial Center for Disease Control is assessing risk factors to guide a coordinated response. Vietnam continues to report approximately 70–100 rabies deaths annually, underscoring the critical need for vaccination and responsible pet ownership. The dog involved in the incident was confirmed to have rabies, leading to swift action from health authorities to control the situation and prevent further cases.

article.articleHeadline: Avian Influenza in India: Containment efforts and public health measures intensify
article.articleSummary: An outbreak of avian influenza in Kerala has prompted the culling of over 20,000 birds, primarily in Kozhikode (14,228) and Alappuzha (5,961) districts, due to the highly pathogenic H5N1 strain. Rapid response teams are actively conducting culling operations within a one-kilometer containment zone to curb further spread. In Chennai, Guindy Children's Park has closed following the death of approximately 40 birds, with lab tests confirming H5N1 as the cause. The first fatalities were reported in the Vedanthangal wetland aviary, with additional deaths occurring subsequently. Authorities are closely monitoring the situation, and as of March 21, 2026, no human infections have been linked to these outbreaks. Public health officials are urging vigilance, advising residents to maintain hygiene, avoid raw poultry products, and report unusual bird deaths. The transport and sale of poultry from affected areas are prohibited, and joint assessments by health and animal husbandry departments are ongoing to manage the outbreak effectively.

article.articleHeadline: Chikungunya in Brazil: Emergency measures to combat escalating outbreak
article.articleSummary: As of March 21, 2026, Brazil has reported 504 confirmed cases of chikungunya, marking an 84% increase from 274 cases just two days earlier. The outbreak is particularly severe in Indigenous villages like Jaguapiru and Bororó in Dourados, where four fatalities, including a 3-month-old infant, have been recorded. São Paulo is also facing challenges with 315 confirmed cases and two deaths, exacerbated by rising temperatures that promote mosquito breeding. Dourados has declared a public health emergency due to the chikungunya epidemic, struggling with medicine shortages and inadequate hospital capacity. The crisis is further complicated in Indigenous communities by poor sanitation and lack of potable water, necessitating immediate coordinated action. In Ituiutaba, Minas Gerais, two patients required fire department assistance on March 20 due to severe swelling from the virus. As of March 21, Ituiutaba reports 1,052 probable and 323 confirmed cases, with no deaths, while Uberaba has recorded one chikungunya-related death. In response, Sesai has announced the hiring of endemic disease-control agents to strengthen containment efforts.

Health officials are implementing water safety measures and community awareness initiatives while managing the avian flu situation. A tragic case involves a 3.5-year-old girl who died, with several other children showing symptoms and under observation as lab tests are conducted to identify the source.

article.articleSummary: As of March 21, 2026, Vietnam's An Giang Province has reported a fatal case of meningococcal meningitis involving an 11-year-old girl in Phú Quốc, prompting urgent public health measures. The disease, caused by Neisseria meningitidis, has a case fatality rate of 8-10% and can lead to severe neurological complications. Local authorities have restricted gatherings and emphasized hygiene practices, while vaccination efforts have intensified, with many parents seeking immunization for their children. Additionally, another student from the same class has contracted meningococcal meningitis (group B), with health officials enhancing monitoring and vaccination campaigns to prevent further transmission. In 2025, Vietnam reported 95 cases and 3 deaths from meningococcal meningitis, underscoring the ongoing public health challenge.

article.articleHeadline: Dengue in Brazil: Intensified public health efforts amid widespread outbreaks
article.articleSummary: As of March 17, 2026, Brazil is facing a significant dengue outbreak with over 148,000 probable cases reported nationwide. São Paulo has the highest confirmed cases at 15,744, accompanied by 6 fatalities. Piauí, particularly affected, reports 1,895 probable cases, with 852 confirmed as of March 21. The state leads the Northeast with an incidence rate of 56.0 suspected cases per 100,000 population, primarily affecting individuals aged 20-29. Contributing factors include high temperatures and recent flooding, which have created favorable conditions for Aedes aegypti mosquito breeding. Health authorities are conducting weekly inspections and community initiatives to eliminate standing water. A vaccination campaign is in progress, distributing 6,950 doses of a new single-dose vaccine aimed at protecting health workers and vulnerable populations. In addition, Juiz de Fora is experiencing a spike in infectious diseases, including hepatitis A, following floods that resulted in 73 deaths, highlighting the urgent need for public health interventions.

article.articleHeadline: Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) Infection in Brazil: Public health initiatives focus on vulnerable children
article.articleSummary: As of March 21, 2026, Brazil is grappling with significant challenges from Severe Acute Respiratory Infections (SARI), with Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) accounting for 13.4% of cases and 4.5% of related deaths. By mid-March, 29,573 RSV vaccine doses had been administered, alongside prophylactic measures like nirsevimabe. RSV remains the leading cause of severe respiratory infections in infants, with hospitalizations in babies under one year exceeding the previous three-year average, underscoring the urgent need for effective public health strategies to protect vulnerable populations.

article.articleHeadline: Leptospirosis in Brazil: Health alert issued amid flooding and disease spread

triage.notes: 記事はブラジルでのレプトスピラ症アウトブレイクが主題。発生地域フィールドのブラジルが対象国リストに含まれるため verified_locations に含める。洪水による環境汚染が感染拡大の主要因となっており、ヘパチティスAの同時多発も報告されている。保健当局による積極的な対応が実施中。

article.articleHeadline: Meningococcal Disease in Thailand: Monitoring cases and promoting vaccination strategies
article.articleSummary: As of March 18, 2026, Thailand has reported five cases of meningococcal disease, resulting in three fatalities. These cases are not linked to the ongoing outbreak in the United Kingdom, which has seen approximately 20 cases and two deaths. The Department of Disease Control is actively monitoring the situation, particularly the Neisseria meningitidis serogroup B (MenB) outbreak in the UK. Health authorities in Thailand emphasize the importance of immediate reporting of suspected cases to facilitate rapid investigations and prevent further spread. Symptoms to be aware of include sudden high fever, severe headache, neck stiffness, and potential rash. Vaccination, particularly the MenB vaccine, is highly recommended for travelers, ideally administered at least 10 days prior to travel to high-risk areas. Public health measures include promoting hand hygiene, wearing masks in crowded settings, and avoiding close respiratory contact. For assistance, the public can contact the health hotline at 1422.

triage.headline_ja: タイにおける髄膜炎菌感染症：症例の監視とワクチン接種戦略の推進
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準で3項目該当（深刻な公衆衛生への影響：死亡例3件、異常性：国内発生クラスター、国際的拡大リスク：UK発生との関連注視）。WPROスクリーニング基準では重症度（死亡率60%）と流行しやすさ（ヒト-ヒト感染性の高い髄膜炎菌）が該当。政府レベル（保健当局）の能動的な監視と国際的関心がある。
triage.notes: タイで確認された5症例（死亡3件）はUK発生と無関連とされているが、タイ保健当局がUK MenB発生を積極的に監視していることが記事で明示されている。髄膜炎菌はヒト-ヒト感染の高いリスク病原体であり、死亡率が高い（確認症例中60%）。ワクチン推奨・公衆衛生メッセージの発信が開始されている。

article.articleHeadline: Shigellosis in India: Health authorities implement urgent measures to control spread
article.articleSummary: An outbreak of Shigellosis has emerged in Peruvayal Panchayat, Kozhikode district, Kerala, with 51 individuals currently under observation and one confirmed hospitalization. Tragically, a 3.5-year-old girl has died from suspected Shigella infection, prompting local health officials to intensify surveillance and public health measures. Authorities are conducting community awareness campaigns and enhancing water safety protocols, as the source of the outbreak remains unidentified. Drinking water and food samples are being tested for contamination. Symptoms of Shigellosis include diarrhea, fever, stomach cramps, and fatigue, with severe dehydration being a significant risk without treatment. Residents are advised to boil drinking water and report symptoms to health officials. The outbreak coincides with ongoing avian influenza cases in the region, leading to additional public health challenges. Health officials emphasize the importance of hygiene practices, including proper handwashing and safe food handling, to prevent further transmission, particularly among high-risk groups such as children under five.

triage.headline_ja: インドのシゲラ症：保健当局が拡大防止への緊急措置を実施
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準3つ該当（重篤な影響・異常性・国際拡大リスク）、WPRO基準3つ該当（重症度・長期曝露・流行しやすさ）、死亡例を伴う集団発生事例。
triage.notes: ケーラ州コージコード地区Peruvayal Panchayatでのシゲラ症集団発生。51人が観察下、1人が入院、3.5歳女児の死亡確認。水源汚染が疑われており、飲料水の煮沸指導が発出。同地域での鳥インフルエンザの同時発生も公衆衛生上の複合課題。

article.articleHeadline: Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) Infection in Vietnam: Strategies to address rising infection rates and vulnerabilities
article.articleSummary: Vietnam anticipates a significant increase in Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) infections, particularly among children and the elderly. The Ministry of Health's 2026 Infectious Disease Prevention Plan estimates approximately 4.5 million RSV infections from 2020 to 2025, with the CDC projecting 3.6 to 6.5 million outpatient visits and 190,000 to 350,000 hospitalizations in the upcoming seasons. The mortality rate associated with RSV is concerning, with estimates of 10,000 to 23,000 deaths annually in the U.S. alone. A recent respiratory conference in Ho Chi Minh City highlighted the 'double burden' faced by the elderly, where 87.7% have chronic diseases that heighten their vulnerability to both RSV and Streptococcus pneumoniae infections. The government is focusing on early risk assessment, integrated prevention strategies, and community awareness initiatives to mitigate the impact of RSV and related respiratory infections, emphasizing the need for holistic respiratory care and stronger public-private collaboration.

triage.headline_ja: ベトナムにおける呼吸器合胞体ウイルス(RSV)感染症：上昇する感染率と脆弱性に対処する戦略
triage.triage_reason: ベトナムにおけるRSV感染症の大幅な増加予測が報告され、IHR基準（重大な公衆衛生への影響、国際的拡大リスク）を満たす。WPRO基準では重症度（高い死亡率と入院数）と流行しやすさ（易感染性集団への影響）が該当し、シグナルとして識別すべき。
triage.notes: 記事サマリーはベトナムにおけるRSV感染症の公衆衛生上の脅威を述べており、ベトナム保健省の2026年感染症予防計画に基づいて推定される感染数（450万件）および入院者数（19万～35万件）は顕著。高齢者と慢性疾患保有者が特に脆弱であり、政府による統合的予防戦略が検討されている。ただし、CDCの予測数はUS向けのものであり、ベトナム固有のデータと混在している点に注意。

article.articleHeadline: Influenza A in Brazil: Surveillance heightened amid seasonal respiratory infections
article.articleSummary: The H5N2 subtype of Influenza A has been detected in the Brazilian Pantanal, marking the first instance of this avian influenza virus in local bird populations. A study involving 1,108 samples from 157 bird species confirmed the presence of AIV RNA in Charadrius collaris, with genetic analysis showing a 94% similarity to H5N2 strains from Colombia. While no human cases have been reported, this finding emphasizes the need for continued avian influenza monitoring in South America. Concurrently, 20 Brazilian states, including Acre, are on alert for Severe Acute Respiratory Infection (SARI) activity, with influenza A identified as a leading cause of severe illness among vulnerable populations. As of March 2026, Brazil has recorded 20,311 SARI cases, with 21.8% testing positive for influenza A, which has increased to 25.4% in recent weeks. Vaccination efforts for influenza A are set to begin on March 28, targeting priority groups across various regions.

triage.headline_ja: ブラジルにおけるインフルエンザA：季節性呼吸器感染症の中での監視体制強化
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準で2つ以上該当（異常性・予想外性、国際的拡大リスク）。H5N2鳥インフルエンザの初検出と複数州でのSARI増加が同時に報告されており、動物・ヒト両方への影響がある。
triage.notes: H5N2鳥インフルエンザがブラジルのパンタナル地域で初検出され、コロンビアの株との94%の類似性を示している。同時にSARI患者数が増加（21.8%がインフルエンザA陽性）し、複数州で警戒が敷かれている。人感染はまだ報告されていないが、監視強化とワクチン接種開始（3月28日）が計画されている。南米での鳥インフルエンザ監視体制の強化が求められる段階と判断される。

article.articleHeadline: Influenza in Brazil: Vaccination campaigns aim to curb rising infections
article.articleSummary: Influenza A cases are on the rise across Brazil, particularly in regions such as Mato Grosso, the Northeast (excluding Piauí), and parts of the North and Southeast, including Rio de Janeiro and Espírito Santo. In 2026, the predominant causes of Severe Acute Respiratory Infection (SARI) cases are Rhinovirus, followed by Influenza A and SARS-CoV-2. Recent statistics show that SARS-CoV-2 accounts for 37.3% of deaths, while Influenza A contributes to 28.6%. In the last four weeks, both Influenza A and SARS-CoV-2 have been linked to 30.8% of positive deaths. To address this, the Fiocruz research team has proposed three national strategies to enhance vaccination coverage and reduce hospitalizations. The influenza vaccination campaign for priority groups is set from March 28 to May 30, with a national mobilization event on March 28. In Acre, low vaccination rates for the influenza trivalent vaccine have been reported, with only 7.79% of children and 7.01% of the elderly vaccinated as of November 2025. Despite a slight uptick in SRAG hospitalizations, deaths have decreased from previous years.

triage.headline_ja: ブラジルのインフルエンザ：感染者数の増加に対応するためワクチン接種キャンペーン実施
triage.triage_reason: ブラジル全土でインフルエンザA症例が増加しており、異常性と重症度の要素は認められるが、死亡数は前年比で減少しており、国内対応能力が示唆されている。国際的拡大リスクおよび渡航・貿易制限のリスクは現在低いと評価される。継続的な監視が必要。
triage.notes: IHR基準は2つ該当し、WPRO基準は4つ該当している。ブラジル政府がワクチン接種キャンペーンを組織し、Fiocruzが全国戦略を提案するなど、社会的・政治的関心は高い。ただし死亡数が前年比で減少しており、完全なフルRRAには至らないため、継続観察段階として判定した。

article.articleHeadline: Tuberculosis in Thailand: AI technologies improve TB detection and diagnosis
article.articleSummary: In 2024, Thailand is grappling with an estimated 104,000 tuberculosis (TB) cases, with only about 81,700 diagnosed and treated, leaving approximately 22,300 individuals undiagnosed. Although there has been a slight decline of 2% in TB cases from 2023 to 2024, this progress falls short of the goal to eliminate TB by 2030. The country remains classified as a high-burden nation for both TB and TB-HIV, while drug-resistant TB is no longer among the highest burdens. The adoption of upfront molecular testing has surged to 69%, exceeding the global average of 54%, with a target to fully replace microscopy by 2027. AI-assisted screening technologies, such as Genki AI, which received FDA approval in Thailand, are significantly enhancing early detection, including for asymptomatic cases. At Chonburi’s Aikchol Hospital, radiologist Dr. Grisit Prueksaritanond utilizes Genki AI to interpret chest X-rays, successfully identifying TB-related lesions and improving diagnostic accuracy, thereby preventing missed cases.

triage.headline_ja: タイの結核：AI技術がTB検出と診断を改善
triage.triage_reason: 本記事はタイにおける結核の疫学的状況とAI診断技術の導入に関するニュースであり、新たな感染症アウトブレイクやシグナル検知の対象ではない。IHR基準・スクリーニング基準に該当せず、社会的関心も限定的。
triage.notes: 記事は既知の結核負荷国（タイ）における診断技術の進展を報じたもので、新規アウトブレイク、異常な疫学的変化、または感染症危機の兆候を示すシグナルではない。年間推定10万4000例という数字は常態的な高負荷状況であり、検出率の改善は公衆衛生改善の報告である。

article.articleHeadline: Cholera in Democratic Republic of the Congo: Health system under strain from multiple epidemics
article.articleSummary: As of March 21, 2026, the Democratic Republic of the Congo has reported 484 cholera deaths amid ongoing outbreaks, contributing to a total of 18,500 suspected cases and 5,300 confirmed cases across Africa this year. The case fatality rate stands at 2.03%. The Lisala Health Zone in Mongala Province is particularly affected, facing concurrent epidemics of cholera, measles, and mpox. Since July 2025, cholera has persisted, worsened by inadequate access to clean water and limited health resources. Authorities have attempted to mitigate the situation by distributing household chlorine and conducting disinfection efforts, but the death toll continues to rise. In addition to cholera, the region has reported 111 measles cases with 9 fatalities since January 2026. The health system is under significant strain, necessitating urgent logistical support to address these public health challenges and prevent further mortality.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のコレラ：複数の流行で保健システムが逼迫
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準4項目すべてに該当し、複数の流行の並行発生、高い死亡数、限定的な資源環境での継続的な発生が確認される。WPROスクリーニング基準も全て該当。
triage.notes: 2026年3月時点でアフリカ全体で18,500疑似患者、5,300確認患者が報告されており国際的な拡大リスクが高い。リサラ保健圏ではコレラ、麻疹、mpoxの3つの流行が並行発生。2025年7月からの継続的な発生、水へのアクセス不良、保健資源の限界が状況を悪化させている。緊急な国際的支援が必要な段階。

article.articleHeadline: Mpox in Brazil: Ongoing monitoring reveals new cases and investigations
article.articleSummary: As of March 21, 2026, Ceará, Brazil, has confirmed its third Mpox case this year, with a total of 29 notifications reported. Out of these, three cases have been confirmed, while 24 have been discarded after testing, and two remain under investigation. The first two cases were identified in February, with the initial confirmation occurring on March 9. The state's public health dashboard emphasizes the importance of ongoing epidemiological surveillance to detect new infections. Mpox transmission primarily occurs through direct contact with skin lesions and secretions, with respiratory droplets posing a risk during prolonged close exposure. The first confirmed case involved a 37-year-old man who received medical care and is recovering well. Laboratory confirmation relies on molecular testing or genetic sequencing of lesion material, underscoring the need for continued public health efforts in monitoring and managing the situation.

triage.headline_ja: ブラジルのエムポックス：継続的な監視で新規症例と調査が明らかに
triage.triage_reason: ブラジルはBluedotの対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations は空となり、PICKUP基準を満たさない。ただしエムポックスは国際的に重要な感染症であり、継続的な情報収集が必要。
triage.notes: ブラジルはトリアージ対象国リストに含まれていないため、本シグナルは地域検証段階で除外される。ただし、エムポックスの流行傾向監視という観点からは関心を持つべき情報である。Ceará州で3例確定、29件の通知、24件を除外、2件は調査中という状況が報告されている。

article.articleHeadline: Hepatitis A in Brazil: Flooding exacerbates outbreak and health challenges
article.articleSummary: As of March 19, 2026, Juiz de Fora in Minas Gerais has reported 248 cases of hepatitis A, reflecting a dramatic 6,100% increase from just four cases during the same period last year. This outbreak follows severe flooding in the Zona da Mata region, which has also resulted in 73 deaths. The transmission of hepatitis A is linked to contaminated food and water, as well as close contact among individuals in crowded conditions. In response, vaccination efforts have been intensified, targeting pregnant women and individuals aged 11-39 who are household or sexual contacts of confirmed cases. The state has allocated 10,000 vaccine doses for Juiz de Fora and 5,000 for Ubá, along with 17,500 bottles of sodium hypochlorite for water purification. Additionally, the federal government has provided health kits for 13,500 individuals and enhanced surveillance measures. In Ubá, eight flood-related deaths have been reported, and leptospirosis remains a significant health concern, with 118 suspected cases.

triage.headline_ja: ブラジルのA型肝炎：洪水が流行と健康課題を悪化させる
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準3項目該当（深刻な公衆衛生影響・異常・国際拡大リスク）、WPRO基準4項目該当（重症度・長期曝露・流行性・管理課題）、社会的関心も高い。洪水による衛生環境悪化で急速に拡大するA型肝炎の流行シグナルとして識別される。
triage.notes: 2026年3月21日時点の情報。前年同期比6,100%の急増（4例→248例）は異常値。洪水による衛生悪化が感染拡大の直接的原因。水・食物媒介性とヒト-ヒト感染の両方が存在。政府レベルの対応（ワクチン、衛生物資配付）が開始されており、管理可能性に課題あり。複合災害（洪水+感染症）の文脈であるため、注視の必要性高い。

article.articleHeadline: Tuberculosis in Philippines: Efforts to enhance detection and treatment strategies
article.articleSummary: The National Capital Region (NCR) of the Philippines has reported a total of 101,807 tuberculosis (TB) cases, highlighting a significant health challenge in Metro Manila. As World TB Day approaches on March 24, the Department of Health - Metro Manila Center for Health Development (DOH-MMCHD) is intensifying efforts for early detection through enhanced screening initiatives. Regional Director Lester Tan emphasized the importance of prompt diagnosis and treatment, warning that delays can worsen health outcomes. To raise awareness and encourage testing, the DOH-MMCHD has organized a TB-Free Generation Fun Run in Taguig City. The ongoing public health campaigns focus on TB surveillance, community engagement, and timely treatment to reduce transmission rates and improve overall health in the region.

triage.headline_ja: フィリピンの結核：検出と治療戦略の強化への取り組み
triage.triage_reason: フィリピンの首都圏で101,807件の結核患者が報告され、異常性と重症度が認められるが、既知の感染症対応中であり国際的拡大リスクの記述が不足しているため、追加情報を注視する必要がある。
triage.notes: 結核は既知の感染症であり通常予想される疾患である。しかし10万件超の患者報告数、地域での持続的曝露、ヒト-ヒト感染の可能性、政府による能動的な公衆衛生対応が確認される。World TB Dayに関連した意識啓発活動も社会的関心を示している。国際的拡大リスクや貿易制限リスクについては記事に記載されていない。

article.articleHeadline: Mpox in India: Emerging variant raises global health alarms
article.articleSummary: A new recombinant variant of mpox, combining elements from clades Ib and IIb, has emerged, prompting significant concern from the World Health Organization (WHO). The first case in India was reported in 2025, with subsequent cases linked to travel in the UK, indicating potential transmission across multiple countries. This variant complicates detection and control efforts, as conventional PCR methods failed to identify it, necessitating whole-genome sequencing for confirmation. Recent studies have raised questions about the effectiveness of tecovirimat, the primary antiviral treatment, which showed no significant improvement in recovery times for immunocompetent patients. The WHO is advocating for enhanced global surveillance and research to address the evolving nature of the virus, emphasizing the importance of updated treatment strategies and vaccination efforts, particularly for vulnerable populations. As of March 21, 2026, the situation remains critical, with ongoing monitoring required to manage the risks associated with this new strain.

triage.headline_ja: インドのMpox：新興変異株が世界的な保健上の警報を引き起こす
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準3つ該当（異常性、国際的拡大リスク、国際支援の必要性）、WPRO基準全5つ該当。新規組換え変異株の出現、複数国での検出、従来の診断法の限界、抗ウイルス治療の効果低下などが示唆されている。フルRRAが必要。
triage.notes: 記事サマリーでインドでの初症例報告（2025年）、UK関連の渡航関連症例、複数国への拡大の可能性が明記されている。新規Ib/IIb組換え変異株、既存PCRでの検出失敗、tecovirimat有効性の低下など、複数の深刻な知見が含まれている。2026年3月21日時点での評価。

article.articleHeadline: Human Infection with Avian Influenza A H5N1 in India: Containment measures and public safety protocols enforced
article.articleSummary: Avian influenza A H5N1 has been confirmed in Kozhikode district, Kerala, leading to the culling of approximately 15,000 birds across five panchayats: Panangad, Olavanna, Kakkodi, Perumanna, and Nallalam. This proactive measure aims to prevent the spread of the highly pathogenic virus, which has been identified through laboratory testing. Currently, there are no reported human infections, and health officials maintain that the situation is under control. Enhanced surveillance and precautionary measures are being implemented, including public advisories against touching dead or sick birds. The Animal Husbandry Department has deployed rapid-response teams, and the transport and sale of poultry from the affected areas are prohibited. Joint assessments by health and animal husbandry departments are ongoing to monitor the situation closely. Authorities emphasize the importance of vigilance and reporting any unusual bird deaths to veterinary services.

triage.headline_ja: インドにおける鳥インフルエンザA H5N1ヒト感染：封じ込め対策と公衆衛生プロトコールの実施
triage.triage_reason: H5N1の高病原性ウイルスが確認されケララ州で約15,000羽の鳥の処分が実施されている異常事象だが、現時点でヒト感染報告なく重症度基準が未充足。情報充実後の展開監視が必要。
triage.notes: 現在のところヒト感染は報告されていないが、H5N1は高い病原性を持ち、ヒト感染リスクが存在する。ケララ州およびタミル・ナドゥ州での大規模なウイルス検出と防疫措置は社会的関心が高く、今後の感染状況（特にヒト感染の有無）の推移を注視する必要がある。

article.articleHeadline: Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) Infection in Brazil: Increased SARI cases and vaccination efforts underway
article.articleSummary: As of Week 10 (March 8–14), 2026, Acre is one of 20 Brazilian states on alert for Severe Acute Respiratory Infection (SARI) activity, according to Fiocruz InfoGripe. The country has reported a total of 20,311 SARI cases, with 37% testing positive for respiratory viruses. Among these, rhinovirus accounts for 41.9%, influenza A for 21.8%, Covid-19 for 14.7%, and RSV for 13.4%. The rise in influenza A cases, which has increased to 25.4% of positives in the last four weeks, is concerning, especially as RSV continues to contribute to severe cases in children under 2 years old in Acre and other Northern states. Vaccination efforts are set to begin on March 28, targeting priority groups for influenza A, while an RSV vaccine for pregnant women is also being introduced. The situation remains dynamic as Brazil approaches the peak respiratory virus season.

article.articleHeadline: COVID-19 in Brazil: Monitoring respiratory infections ahead of autumn season
article.articleSummary: Acre is one of 20 Brazilian states currently on alert for Severe Acute Respiratory Infection (SARI) activity, as reported by Fiocruz InfoGripe for Week 10 (March 8–14). The country is witnessing an increase in influenza A cases, which is expected to peak during the autumn season. In Acre and other Northern states, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is contributing to severe cases among children under two. The latest data shows that Brazil recorded 20,311 SARI cases in 2026, with 37% testing positive for a respiratory virus. Among the positive cases, rhinovirus accounted for 41.9%, influenza A for 21.8%, and COVID-19 for 14.7%. Although COVID-19 persists at lower levels, it remains concentrated in the Southeast region. Vaccination efforts are set to begin on March 28, targeting priority groups for influenza A and introducing an RSV vaccine for pregnant women.

triage.headline_ja: ブラジルのCOVID-19：秋季に向けた呼吸器感染症の監視
triage.triage_reason: ブラジルで複数の呼吸器感染症（SARI）が増加中であり、COVID-19も検出されているが、現在の感染レベルは低く、重症度や国際的拡大の危険性は明確でない。情報不足のため経過観察が適切。
triage.notes: 記事はブラジルの複数州（アクレ、ロライマ、アマゾナス、ロンドニア、パラ）でSARI活動が増加していることを報告。COVID-19は検出されているが全体の14.7%に過ぎず、現在の主要な懸念はインフルエンザAとRSV。ブラジル政府は監視と予防接種対応を行っており、管理能力は十分と判断される。

article.articleHeadline: Influenza B in Brazil: SARI cases prompt vaccination efforts across the country
article.articleSummary: As of Week 10 (March 8–14), Brazil reports 20,311 cases of Severe Acute Respiratory Infection (SARI), with 37% testing positive for respiratory viruses. Among these, influenza A accounts for 21.8% of positive cases, while influenza B is noted at 1.5%. The data indicates a concerning trend, particularly in Acre and 19 other states, where SARI activity is classified as alert/high risk by Fiocruz InfoGripe. The rise in influenza A cases, which has increased to 25.4% of positives in the last four weeks, is particularly alarming as the country approaches its peak respiratory illness season. Vaccination campaigns are set to begin on March 28, targeting priority groups in various regions, with a specific focus on influenza A and RSV, especially for vulnerable populations such as pregnant women. The ongoing presence of rhinovirus and lower levels of Covid-19 further complicate the respiratory illness landscape in Brazil.

triage.headline_ja: ブラジルのインフルエンザB：SARI症例が全国の予防接種努力を促す
triage.triage_reason: インフルエンザBの流行が報告されているが、サマリーではインフルエンザAが主要な懸念（21.8%→25.4%）であり、インフルエンザBは1.5%と低い割合。複数州での高リスク警報が出ているが、国家的な対応（ワクチン接種キャンペーン）が既に計画されており、重大度や国際的拡大の具体的リスクが不明。
triage.notes: 記事サマリーではインフルエンザAが主要な懸念であり、インフルエンザBは1.5%と低い割合であることに注意。複数州（Acre、Roraima、Amazonas等）での高リスク警報が出ており、呼吸器疾患のシーズンピークに向かっている。政府は既に3月28日のワクチン接種キャンペーンを計画している。国際的拡大のリスクと外部支援の必要性については記事に記載がない。

article.articleHeadline: Tuberculosis in Philippines: Intensified efforts to combat high case numbers
article.articleSummary: As of February 16, 2026, Metro Manila has reported 101,807 tuberculosis cases, according to the Department of Health (DOH) via the Integrated Tuberculosis Information System. In response to this significant public health challenge, the DOH is ramping up efforts for early detection, prompt treatment, and prevention strategies. In 2025, over 3.1 million residents in Metro Manila were screened for TB, highlighting the urgency of addressing this issue. Key symptoms to monitor include a persistent cough lasting two weeks or more, chest pain, fever, weakness, night sweats, and unexplained weight loss. The DOH is promoting TB Preventive Treatment for high-risk groups, particularly children and other vulnerable populations, to prevent the progression to active TB and reduce community transmission. These measures aim to enhance treatment outcomes and curb the spread of the disease.

triage.headline_ja: フィリピンの結核：高い症例数に対抗するための強化された取り組み
triage.triage_reason: 結核は慢性疾患であり、メトロマニラで10万以上の累積症例が報告されているが、突発的な流行や国際的拡大の直接的な証拠は記事に示されていない。公衆衛生上の課題は明らかだが、IHR基準（特に国際的拡大リスク）の判定に必要な情報が不足している。
triage.notes: 結核は既知の地域的課題であり、新規の異常な流行状況ではない。DOHによる予防戦略の強化は管理可能な対応と判断される。続報で急速な流行拡大や治療耐性株の出現などが報告される場合はピックアップへ昇格の可能性あり。

article.articleHeadline: HIV in India: Youth infections prompt urgent government intervention
article.articleSummary: Gurugram has been designated a priority area for HIV control by the central government due to a concerning increase in infections among the youth. The National Aids Control Organisation (NACO) has identified Gurugram as one of 11 districts in Haryana and 219 nationwide that require intensified intervention. Currently, 2,770 individuals living with HIV are receiving treatment in the district. The government's strategy includes expanding testing, counselling, and treatment services to effectively reduce transmission rates. Health authorities are focusing on enhancing public health measures and resource allocation to address the rising burden among young people. As of March 22, 2026, efforts are underway to improve prevention, diagnosis, and management of HIV, with plans for increased outreach and linkage-to-care across local clinics.

triage.headline_ja: インドのHIV：青年層の感染急増が緊急政府介入を促す
triage.triage_reason: HIV感染は既知の風土病であり、青年層での増加は重要だが、新規・異常な病原体や急速な国際拡大のリスクは示唆されていない。ただし、政府による優先地域指定と積極的対応の必要性から経過観察の価値がある。
triage.notes: HIVは既知の慢性感染症であり、IHR基準の『異常・予想外』には該当しない。ただしWPRO基準で重症度・長期曝露・流行しやすさに該当し、インド政府による正式な優先地域指定と積極的介入戦略が確認されている。2026年時点での時系列は将来の仮定値であるため、現況把握の観点からWATCHレベルが適切。

article.articleHeadline: Mpox in Brazil: First confirmed case prompts health monitoring efforts
article.articleSummary: The first mpox case of 2026 has been confirmed in Brasiléia, Acre, as reported by Sesacre on March 17. The infection is classified as imported, with no local transmission detected. The patient is currently under health surveillance, and authorities are emphasizing laboratory confirmation, surveillance, and contact tracing to mitigate any potential spread. Health officials are particularly vigilant regarding travel-related mpox cases in northern Brazil. As of the latest updates, no additional cases or deaths have been reported in Acre.

triage.headline_ja: ブラジルのエンポックス：最初の確認症例が保健監視活動を促す
triage.triage_reason: ブラジルにおける2026年初のエンポックス輸入症例が確認されたが、地域内伝播は未検出で死亡なし。情報の確実性と国際的拡大リスクが不明なため、今後の発展を注視する必要がある。
triage.notes: 記事サマリーではブラジル（アクレ州ブラジレイア）での輸入症例と明記されており、地域内伝播なし・死亡ゼロとのことで、現時点でのリスク水準は限定的。ただし、北部ブラジルにおける渡航関連症例への警戒が示唆されているため、続報の監視推奨。

article.articleHeadline: Dengue in Brazil: Climate conditions heighten outbreak concerns
article.articleSummary: Dengue in Brazil continues to pose a significant threat, with experts cautioning that recent declines in cases do not eliminate the risk of new outbreaks. The potential for increased transmission is heightened by the anticipated return of El Niño conditions, which could create a favorable environment for Aedes aegypti mosquitoes. In 2023, Brazil experienced a notable increase in dengue cases, culminating in the largest burden recorded in 2024. While vaccination efforts are underway, they cannot substitute for essential vector control measures. Authorities stress the importance of preventive actions such as eliminating standing water and maintaining clean environments to mitigate risks. Despite current indicators showing lower case counts, the threat of outbreaks remains, influenced by climate variability and the effectiveness of mosquito control strategies. Ongoing surveillance and vaccination initiatives are critical as Brazil navigates these challenges.

triage.headline_ja: ブラジルのデング熱：気候条件が感染症流行への懸念を高める
triage.triage_reason: デング熱は既知の風土病であり、現在の症例数は減少傾向を示している。ただし、エルニーニョ現象の予想される戻りによるリスク増加の可能性があり、予防的監視と情報の追跡が必要。
triage.notes: デング熱はブラジルの風土病であり、現在は症例数が低下傾向を示している。記事の焦点は将来のリスク（エルニーニョによる媒介蚊の増加）に関するもので、現在の流行を示すものではない。WPROスクリーニング基準では長期曝露と流行しやすさの2項目が該当するが、IHR基準には該当せず、重大な新規流行シグナルではなく、予防的監視の段階。

article.articleHeadline: Human Infection with Avian Influenza in India: Public health measures intensify amid ongoing outbreaks
article.articleSummary: As of March 22, 2026, Kozhikode district in Kerala is facing a Shigella infection outbreak, with 51 individuals under observation and one hospitalized. The source of the outbreak remains unknown, prompting public health authorities to implement intensified surveillance and awareness campaigns. Concurrently, the Rapid Response Team (RRT) is expanding preventive measures in areas previously affected by avian influenza, including recent poultry culling in four panchayats and the Nallalam division. The Animal Husbandry Department and the District Collectorate are actively coordinating control efforts, advising those in contact with poultry to remain vigilant and report any symptoms. A prohibition on the sale and use of poultry within a 10-km radius of the outbreak's origin has been established to mitigate further spread.

triage.headline_ja: インドの鳥インフルエンザ人感染：継続的な流行の中で公衆衛生対策が強化
triage.triage_reason: 記事サマリーの主題はシゲラ感染症のアウトブレイク（51人が観察対象、1人入院）であり、見出しと疾患名（鳥インフルエンザ）との乖離がある。鳥インフルエンザについては過去の影響範囲への予防対策拡大の記述に留まり、現在の人感染事例の詳細が不明。情報整合性の確認と続報の経過観察が必要。
triage.notes: 【重要な不一致】Bluedot APIの疾患名は『鳥インフルエンザ人感染』だが、記事サマリーの主要内容はシゲラ感染症のアウトブレイク（Kozhikode地区、51人観察中）。鳥インフルエンザについてはKerala州での過去の影響範囲における予防対策の拡大（家禽の淘汰、10km以内の家禽販売禁止）として言及されているに過ぎない。記事がシゲラ感染症とも鳥インフルエンザの新規人感染についても不確定な情報を報告している。情報精緻化のため継続的な監視が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Dengue in Vietnam: Current trends and hotspots in disease transmission
article.articleSummary: Ho Chi Minh City reported a 14.4% decrease in dengue cases during week 11 (March 9–15), with 582 new cases, bringing the cumulative total to 12,202 for the year. Notable hotspots with dengue incidence exceeding 100 per 100,000 residents include An Nhon Tay, Tay Thanh, and Tay Nam. In contrast, hand-foot-mouth disease (HFMD) cases surged by 97.1% to 837 in the same week, with a cumulative total of 7,294 cases for 2026. HFMD primarily affects children under five and is characterized by blister-like lesions. Preventive measures focus on hygiene practices such as regular handwashing and cleaning shared items to curb transmission. The dual challenge of dengue and HFMD highlights the need for continued public health vigilance in the region.

article.articleHeadline: Enterovirus 71 in Vietnam: Significant increase in hand-foot-mouth disease cases
article.articleSummary: In Ho Chi Minh City, hand-foot-mouth disease (HFMD) cases surged by 97.1% in week 11, totaling 837 reported cases, with a cumulative count of 7,294 for the year 2026. The outbreak primarily affects children under five, presenting with blister-like lesions on various body parts. Key hotspots for HFMD include Long Huong, Long Dien, and Thuong Tan. The disease is transmitted through fecal-oral routes and direct contact with infected secretions. Preventive measures are crucial, emphasizing regular handwashing, cleaning of toys and surfaces, and minimizing the sharing of personal items. Parents are advised to keep symptomatic children at home and notify schools to prevent further spread.

triage.headline_ja: ベトナムのエンテロウイルス71：手足口病の症例が著しく増加

article.articleHeadline: Human Infection with Avian Influenza A H5N1 in India: Intensified control measures amid local outbreaks

Symptoms in humans may include fever, body aches, cough, and respiratory issues. Authorities recommend thorough cooking of poultry products to prevent infection.

article.articleHeadline: Rabies in Vietnam: Urgent response to recent dog attacks reported
article.articleSummary: In Dak Lak, Vietnam, a rabies outbreak has prompted urgent action after six residents were bitten by a suspected rabid dog in mid-March. The dog, owned by a local resident, attacked two children before turning on the owner and three neighbors. A second dog displaying rabies-like symptoms had previously died in early February after biting other dogs. Veterinary officials have collected samples for testing, with results pending. The provincial CDC has directed the victims to receive rabies vaccinations at the Tay Nguyen Institute of Hygiene and Epidemiology, and by March 22, all six individuals had been vaccinated, with five receiving rabies immunoglobulin. Authorities are monitoring other potentially affected dogs and have initiated campaigns to confine pets and vaccinate local dogs and cats. This incident marks the first suspected rabies cluster in the Thanh Cong hamlet this year, highlighting the critical need for prompt medical attention following animal bites, as rabies is nearly always fatal once symptoms manifest.

triage.headline_ja: ベトナムの狂犬病：最近の犬咬傷事件への緊急対応が報告される
triage.triage_reason: ベトナムでの狂犬病集団感染事例であり、6名の被咬傷者、死亡リスクのある重篤疾患、複数の動物咬傷、地域内での継続的な曝露リスク、および公衆衛生当局による積極的な対応が確認される。IHR基準（異常性・予想外性、重症度、国際的拡大の可能性）とWPRO基準（異常性、重症度、継続的曝露、管理対応）の複数項目に該当。
triage.notes: 記事はダク・ラク州（記事サマリー記載）およびンゲアン省の地域での狂犬病事例を報告している。複数の動物咬傷による集団感染、重篤疾患（狂犬病は発症後ほぼ致死的）、地域内での継続的な動物曝露リスク、および迅速なワクチン接種を含む当局の対応が確認される。ベトナムは対象国に含まれるため、フルRRAへの進行を推奨。

article.articleHeadline: Syphilis in Brazil: New strategies for STI prevention and treatment
article.articleSummary: Brazil is addressing the growing challenge of syphilis through innovative public health strategies. Recent reports from Campinas highlight the emergence of superbug infections, specifically KCP, at a municipal hospital, raising concerns about hospital-associated multidrug-resistant infections. In response, the Brazilian Health Ministry has incorporated DoxiPEP (doxycycline post-exposure prophylaxis) into the Unified Health System (SUS) to prevent sexually transmitted infections, including syphilis and chlamydia. This initiative is part of a broader effort to enhance access to medicines and improve STI prevention measures. Additionally, a recent health mutirão focused on women's health was conducted, emphasizing the importance of targeted health interventions. The ongoing collaboration with a Chinese company aims to bolster the domestic production of essential medicines, further supporting Brazil's public health infrastructure. These developments reflect a comprehensive approach to tackling syphilis and other STIs in the country.

triage.headline_ja: ブラジルの梅毒：STI予防と治療の新戦略
triage.triage_reason: 梅毒の公衆衛生対応の報道だが、新規の疾病発生クラスターまたは異常な流行の明確な証拠が不明。予防戦略の導入は制度的進展であり、緊急性の高いシグナルには該当しない。
triage.notes: 記事はブラジルの梅毒対策について報道しており、Campinasでの薬剤耐性菌感染も言及されている。しかし発生地域にBrazilが含まれていながら、verified_locationsが空配列となっている理由：評価対象国リスト（Zambia, Philippines, Thailand, Ghana, DRC, Brazil, Indonesia, China, Myanmar, Vietnam, India）にはBrazilが含まれるが、記事サマリーを詳細に検証すると、この記事の主題は「ブラジルの既存の梅毒流行への制度的対応」であり、新規の異常な疾患クラスターの発生ではなく、むしろ既知の課題に対する予防戦略の導入を報道している。Bluedot APIの「発生地域」フィールドの誤りパターンを考慮し、シグナルトリアージの対象は「新規または異常な感染症イベント」とすべきため、定常的な疾病対応の制度化は対象外と判断した。

article.articleHeadline: Yellow Fever in Philippines: Health alert issued amid confirmed cases and vaccination efforts
article.articleSummary: Aragua state is currently under a health alert for yellow fever, with 36 to 40 laboratory-confirmed cases reported in the last three weeks. The cases are primarily located in southern municipalities, including San Sebastián, San Casimiro, Camatagua, Urdaneta, and urban areas of Zamora/Libertador. Dr. Ramón Rubio, president of the Medical Association, noted that while there have been no official deaths, approximately 80% of patients recover, although 15-20% may experience serious cardiovascular or hepatic complications. A vaccination campaign has been initiated, with over 300 points established to immunize individuals aged 1 to 59 who have not previously received the yellow fever vaccine. Those already vaccinated are advised against revaccination. Additionally, respiratory infections in clinics have decreased from 70% to 40-50%, although influenza A and SARS-CoV-2 continue to circulate. Economic challenges are impacting confirmatory testing, leading to reliance on clinical and laboratory data for diagnosis. The medical sector is advocating for the reopening and expansion of surgical services to address a significant backlog.

triage.headline_ja: フィリピンの黄熱病：確定症例と予防接種活動の中で健康警報が発令
triage.triage_reason: 黄熱病の確定症例（36～40例）が報告され、IHR基準で異常性・重症性・管理困難性が認められ、公衆衛生上の重大な影響がある。ただし記事本文がベネズエラ（アラグア州）の内容であり、見出しと地域情報の不一致に注意が必要。
triage.notes: 重大な矛盾あり：見出しと発生地域指定は「フィリピン」を示唆するが、記事本文はアラグア州（ベネズエラ）での黄熱病流行について述べており、サン・セバスティアン、サン・カシミロ、カマタグア、ウルダネタなどはベネズエラの自治体。フィリピンは対象国リストに含まれるが、実際の発生地はベネズエラ（対象国外）である。したがって verified_locations は空配列。記事の信頼性・正確性の確認が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Human Metapneumovirus Infection in Brazil: Low vaccination rates amid rising respiratory infections
article.articleSummary: As of November 26, 2025, Acre has reported 536 cases of Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome (SRAG) for the year, with the most affected age groups being children aged 0-9 and individuals over 60. The region is experiencing a concerning trend of low vaccination coverage for the influenza trivalent vaccine, with only 7.79% of children, 13.72% of pregnant women, and 7.01% of the elderly vaccinated. Despite a national decline in SRAG hospitalizations, Acre has seen a slight uptick in early 2026, primarily driven by respiratory viruses such as RSV and Rhinovirus. The total number of deaths attributed to SRAG in 2026 stands at 16, a decrease from previous years (29 in 2024 and 45 in 2025). Additionally, consultations for influenza-like illnesses have reached 3,268, indicating ongoing respiratory health challenges in the region.

triage.headline_ja: ブラジルにおけるヒトメタニューモウイルス感染：呼吸器感染症の増加と低いワクチン接種率

triage.notes: 記事サマリーに時間的矛盾がある（配信日2026年3月21日だが、サマリーは2025年11月26日以降のデータを参照）。疾患名はHuman Metapneumovirusとされているが、サマリー内ではSRAG（重症急性呼吸器症候群）、RSV、ライノウイルスが言及されており、メタニューモウイルスの具体的な患者数や重症度については不明。アクレ州での極めて低いワクチン接種率（子ども7.79%、高齢者7.01%）は公衆衛生上の懸念要因。

article.articleHeadline: Human Infection with Swine Influenza A H1N1 in Brazil: Low vaccination rates amid rising respiratory illness cases
article.articleSummary: As of November 26, 2025, Acre has reported 536 cases of Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome (SRAG) for the year, with the most affected age groups being children aged 0-9 and individuals over 60. Hospitalizations have been linked to various respiratory viruses, including Influenza A (H1N1)pdm09. The region is experiencing a concerning trend of low vaccination coverage for the influenza trivalent vaccine, with only 7.79% of children, 13.72% of pregnant women, and 7.01% of the elderly fully vaccinated. Despite a national decline in SRAG cases, Acre has seen a slight uptick in hospitalizations attributed to RSV, Rhinovirus, and Influenza A. The total number of deaths due to SRAG in 2026 stands at 16, a decrease from previous years, indicating some progress, yet the low vaccination rates pose a significant risk for future outbreaks.

article.articleHeadline: HIV in Thailand: AI enhances disease detection in healthcare settings
article.articleSummary: In 2024, Thailand estimates 104,000 individuals will have tuberculosis (TB), with approximately 81,700 expected to be diagnosed and treated, leaving around 22,000 cases undetected. Although Thailand is no longer classified as a high-burden country for drug-resistant TB, it continues to face significant challenges with TB and TB-HIV co-infection. The country has seen a 2% annual decline in TB cases from 2023 to 2024. Notably, the use of upfront molecular testing has increased to 69%, surpassing global and Southeast Asian averages. The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in healthcare, particularly through the Genki AI system, has been pivotal in enhancing TB detection. Approved by the Thai FDA in 2022, Genki AI interprets chest X-rays for TB and other diseases, significantly aiding in the evaluation process at hospitals like Aikchol in Chonburi, where it has helped prevent missed diagnoses of TB cases. This advancement aligns with WHO guidelines promoting AI in TB screening.

triage.headline_ja: タイのHIV：医療現場におけるAIを活用した疾患検出の強化

triage.notes: 記事はタイにおけるAIによる疾患検出の技術的進展についての報道。新規発生、流行拡大、危機的状況の兆候は含まれていない。既存の疾患管理の改善を報告する啓発記事であるため、感染症危機管理シグナルとしての価値はない。

article.articleHeadline: Human Infection with Avian Influenza in Brazil: Monitoring and prevention strategies for H5N1 outbreaks
article.articleSummary: H5N1 high-pathogenic avian influenza has led to the deaths of over 50,000 pinnipeds in South America, including 36,000 South American sea lions, 17,400 southern elephant seals, and 1,000 South American fur seals across Brazil, Peru, Chile, Uruguay, and Argentina. The virus, first detected in marine mammals in 2022, is mutating towards non-avian hosts, with a notable increase in cases in 2023, particularly in Argentina. A study led by UC Davis emphasizes the need for long-term wildlife surveillance, enhanced researcher collaboration, and the integration of wildlife monitoring into conservation efforts. The research advocates for noninvasive monitoring technologies and public policies to address underlying issues such as habitat loss and climate change. Recent sampling efforts in the US aim to track the evolution of the virus in marine mammals and birds, highlighting the urgency of proactive measures to mitigate future outbreaks.

triage.headline_ja: ブラジルにおけるヒトのトリインフルエンザ感染：H5N1アウトブレイクの監視と予防戦略

triage.notes: 記事サマリーはブラジル、ペルー、チリ、ウルグアイ、アルゼンチンにおける海洋哺乳類のH5N1による大量死を報告しているが、対象国リスト内ではブラジルのみが該当。サマリーには現在のヒト感染例の記載がなく、タイトルと内容に不一致がある。病原体の進化とヒト感染リスクの潜在性により、継続的な監視が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Human Infection with Swine Influenza A H1N1 in India: Recent pediatric cases raise public health concerns
article.articleSummary: As of March 21, 2026, Kolkata is experiencing notable swine flu (H1N1) activity, with two children hospitalized and three additional pediatric cases testing positive. Testing is recommended for individuals with persistent symptoms lasting 4–5 days.

article.articleHeadline: Measles in Democratic Republic of the Congo: Concurrent epidemics strain health resources and response efforts
article.articleSummary: Lisala Health Zone in the Mongala Province of the Democratic Republic of Congo is currently grappling with three simultaneous epidemics: measles, cholera, and mpox. Since January 2026, there have been 111 reported cases of measles, resulting in 9 fatalities. Despite efforts to vaccinate contacts of confirmed cases, resource limitations hindered broader vaccination initiatives, contributing to an increase in case fatalities. The cholera outbreak, ongoing since July 2025, has also been severe, with over twenty deaths reported last year due to inadequate access to clean water. Authorities have attempted to mitigate the cholera crisis by distributing household chlorine and conducting disinfection efforts. Meanwhile, mpox continues to pose a threat, with vaccination campaigns in place but limited by resource constraints. The health system in Lisala is under immense pressure as it struggles to manage these outbreaks, prompting urgent calls for logistical support to avert further loss of life.

article.articleHeadline: Pneumococcus in Vietnam: Addressing pneumonia's impact on vulnerable populations
article.articleSummary: Pneumococcal disease remains a primary cause of community-acquired pneumonia in Vietnam, significantly affecting both children and older adults. Recent projections indicate that from 2020 to 2025, nearly 4.5 million acute respiratory infections will occur due to respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), with the CDC estimating 3.6 to 6.5 million outpatient visits, 190,000 to 350,000 hospitalizations, and 10,000 to 23,000 deaths related to these infections. The aging population in Vietnam, with 87.7% of older adults suffering from at least one chronic illness, exacerbates the healthcare burden. Experts at the Ho Chi Minh City Respiratory Society Annual Congress emphasized the need for early risk identification, prevention strategies, and comprehensive respiratory care, alongside enhanced collaboration between public and private sectors to address these challenges effectively.

Experts emphasize the need for comprehensive management strategies and improved implementation of new evidence to mitigate these risks.

article.articleHeadline: Mpox Clade I in Brazil: New recombinant strain raises global health concerns
article.articleSummary: As of March 2025, Brazil has reported cases of mpox clade Ib, particularly in São Paulo, raising alarms about a new recombinant strain of the virus. Detected in February 2026, this strain combines elements from clade Ib, known for its higher severity and mortality rates, especially among vulnerable populations, and clade IIb, which was responsible for the 2022 global outbreak. The World Health Organization (WHO) has expressed concerns about the potential for broader circulation of this recombinant strain, with confirmed cases linked to travel from the UK and India, indicating transmission across multiple countries. Current therapeutic options, such as tecovirimat, have shown limited efficacy in recent trials, prompting a renewed focus on vaccination efforts. Brazil's health authorities are prioritizing vaccination with Jynneos (MVA-BN) through the Unified Health System (SUS) to mitigate the impact of this emerging threat.

article.articleHeadline: Measles in Indonesia: Outbreaks reported across multiple provinces
article.articleSummary: In Indonesia, measles outbreaks have been significant, with 63,769 suspected cases reported in 2025, including 11,094 laboratory-confirmed cases and 69 deaths. By early 2026, the situation remained critical, with 8,224 suspected cases and 572 confirmed cases reported by week 7, resulting in 4 additional deaths. The outbreaks have affected 17 districts across 11 provinces, highlighting the disease's highly contagious nature. Symptoms typically begin with flu-like signs, progressing to a characteristic rash. Complications are severe, particularly among unvaccinated children, leading to conditions such as pneumonia and encephalitis. Preventive measures focus on vaccination, with the MR vaccine recommended at 9 months, followed by boosters at 15–18 months and 5–7 years. Supportive care, including vitamin A supplementation, is crucial for reducing mortality in affected individuals.

triage.notes: 麻しんは高い伝播性を持つ疫病管理可能な感染症であり、予防接種キャンペーンが基本的な対応となる。インドネシアは11州17地区に渡る大規模アウトブレイクを経験中。2025年は69死亡、2026年第7週までに4死亡が報告されている。WPRO地域への重要なシグナル。

article.articleHeadline: Influenza B in Brazil: Widespread activity and vaccination efforts underway
article.articleSummary: As of March 21, 2026, Brazil is experiencing significant circulation of the influenza virus, particularly Influenza A, with a reported 21.8% of Severe Acute Respiratory Infection (SARI) cases attributed to it. Influenza B accounts for only 1.5% of SARI positives, with 2.7% of recent deaths linked to this strain. The most affected regions include Mato Grosso, the Northeast (excluding Piauí), the North (Amapá, Pará, Rondônia), and the Southeast (Rio de Janeiro, Espírito Santo). The Health Ministry has initiated a national vaccination campaign from March 28 to May 30, targeting priority groups to enhance coverage against influenza and RSV. Current mortality statistics show that SARS-CoV-2 and Influenza A are the leading causes of death among respiratory infections, with Influenza B contributing to 2.5% of fatalities. The ongoing vaccination efforts aim to mitigate the impact of these viruses as Brazil navigates this challenging health landscape.

triage.headline_ja: ブラジルのインフルエンザB：広範な活動と予防接種活動が進行中
triage.triage_reason: インフルエンザBはSARI陽性の1.5%にとどまり、死亡の2.7%と限定的。ただしブラジル全域での広範な流行活動と政府の対応が進行中であり、情報更新を注視する必要がある。
triage.notes: 記事ではインフルエンザBが主題だが、実際のサマリーではインフルエンザAが主要な懸念（SARI陽性の21.8%）であり、インフルエンザBの負荷は比較的低い（1.5%）。ただしブラジル保健省による全国予防接種キャンペーン（3月28日～5月30日）が進行中で、複数州での広範な流行が報告されている。目標国外での国際的拡大リスクは記事からは不明。

article.articleHeadline: Tuberculosis in Ghana: Addressing detection gaps and enhancing treatment efforts
article.articleSummary: Ghana's National Tuberculosis Programme reports a significant detection gap, with approximately 20,000 TB cases going untreated each year. The country estimates around 44,000 new TB cases annually, but only 22,000 to 24,000 are identified due to limited capacity, leading to increased community transmission. Pediatric detection is alarmingly low, with only 700 cases identified in 2025, despite expectations of 2,000 annually. To combat this, authorities are ramping up screening efforts in high-risk areas such as prisons, slums, and among individuals living with HIV or poorly controlled diabetes. TB remains a curable disease, with treatment durations of six months for drug-susceptible cases and six to eight months for drug-resistant cases. The programme emphasizes the importance of TB Preventive Therapy for close contacts and high-risk groups, advocating for unified investments in diagnostics and treatment under the theme "Yes, We Can End TB."

triage.headline_ja: ガーナにおける結核：検出ギャップへの対処と治療努力の強化
triage.triage_reason: ガーナで年間約20,000件の未治療結核症例が存在する重大な検出ギャップが報告されており、IHR基準の「深刻な公衆衛生影響」と「異常/予想外」に該当。WPROスクリーニング基準では重症度（未治療症例の多さ）、長期曝露（コミュニティ伝播継続）、管理可能性（容量不足）が該当し、フルRRA進行が必要。
triage.notes: ガーナの国家結核プログラムが公式に報告した検出ギャップ。小児結核検出の異常な低さ（期待値2,000件に対し700件のみ）、HIV患者や糖尿病患者などの高リスク集団への対策強化が進行中。WHO のEnd TB戦略と連動した公式な改善イニシアティブが存在することから、政府レベルでの関心が高い。

article.articleHeadline: Norovirus in Brazil: Outbreak prompts school closures and health measures
article.articleSummary: A gastroenteritis outbreak in Pelotas, southern Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil, has led to the suspension of classes due to a suspected norovirus infection. Currently, 77 cases have been reported among municipal school staff, teachers, and students, with the majority affecting children aged 0–5. Authorities are conducting thorough disinfection of affected facilities and analyzing samples from ten schools at the Central Public Health Laboratory (Lacen), with results anticipated shortly. Norovirus, known for its high contagion rate, causes acute gastroenteritis characterized by symptoms such as low-grade fever, headache, and muscle pains. The transmission occurs primarily through the fecal-oral route, often via contaminated food, water, or surfaces. While there is no specific antiviral treatment, supportive care focusing on hydration and hygiene is recommended. The city assures that the suspension of classes will not disrupt the academic calendar, with activities set to resume following the necessary sanitization efforts.

triage.headline_ja: ブラジルのノロウイルス: 集団発生により学校閉鎖と保健措置
triage.triage_reason: ノロウイルスの学校関連集団発生であり、スクリーニング基準（異常性、流行しやすさ）で2項目該当するが、死亡・重症例の報告がなく、地域的な対応が進行中のため、フルRRA前の情報収集段階が適切。
triage.notes: ブラジルは対象国リストに含まれるため verified_locations に含める。集団発生規模（77例）と学校閉鎖という対応、ノロウイルスの高い伝播性により、WPROスクリーニング基準を複数満たす。ただし重症度情報の欠落と国内対応が進行中のため、PICKUP昇格前に続報監視が適切。

article.articleHeadline: Varicella in India: NHRC demands action on escalating chickenpox cases
article.articleSummary: In January 2026, Kerala reported 3,300 chickenpox cases within the first 24 days, with Kozhikode identified as a significant hotspot, recording 430 cases—more than double the 210 cases reported in December. The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) has intervened, requesting a time-bound action taken report from the Kerala Health Secretary within four weeks, following concerns raised by ETV Bharat regarding the ongoing increase in cases. The data indicates a year-on-year rise in chickenpox cases: 26,390 in 2023, 27,106 in 2024, and 29,055 in 2025. The NHRC emphasized the connection between effective infectious disease control and the fundamental right to life and health, highlighting deficiencies in public health infrastructure, early warning systems, vaccination efforts, isolation protocols, timely medical care, and public awareness initiatives.

triage.headline_ja: インドの水痘：NHRCがコージコード地域の急増する水痘症例への対応を要求

triage.notes: ケーラ州コージコード地域で2026年1月に急速な増加が報告されており（12月の210例から430例へ増加）、年間通じての増加傾向が確認されている（2023年26,390例→2025年29,055例）。NHRCが介入し公衆衛生インフラの欠陥を指摘しているが、死亡例や重症化に関する記述がないため、公衆衛生上の影響度の詳細な評価には情報が不足している。

article.articleHeadline: Tuberculosis in India: Challenges in combating drug-resistant strains
article.articleSummary: India accounts for approximately 25% of global tuberculosis (TB) cases, with a significant burden of multidrug-resistant (MDR) and rifampicin-resistant TB. According to the WHO's Global TB Report 2025, the incidence of TB has declined by 21% from 2015 to 2023, reaching about 187 cases per 100,000 people. However, the target of 44 cases per 100,000 by 2025 remains a distant goal. The country is home to nearly one-third of the world's MDR-TB cases, complicating treatment efforts. Managing drug-resistant TB requires longer treatment durations of 9 to 18 months, often involving second-line drugs that have more severe side effects. The need for rapid molecular diagnostics, such as nucleic acid amplification tests (NAATs), is critical for timely detection of resistance and initiation of appropriate therapy. To address these challenges, India must enhance its National TB Elimination Programme and National Action Plan on Antimicrobial Resistance, ensuring reliable drug procurement, trained healthcare professionals, and effective surveillance systems.

triage.headline_ja: インドにおける結核：薬剤耐性菌株との戦いの課題
triage.triage_reason: インドの結核負担（世界の25%、MDR-TB患者の約3分の1）は深刻だが、記事は主に政策・システム課題の分析であり、急性の新規アウトブレイクやEBS即時対応が必要なシグナルではない。社会的関心は高いが、IHR基準2つ以上の達成は不明確。
triage.notes: 記事はインドの結核対策の構造的課題（MDR-TB管理、診断能力、医療資源）に焦点を当てており、新規の急性流行シグナルではない。既知の慢性的公衆衛生課題の分析・評論的内容。WPROスクリーニング基準では4つ該当するが、異常性が低く、国家プログラム強化を求める政策提言が主題のため、ルーチン監視範囲と判定。続報で新たな耐性株出現やアウトブレイク報告があれば再評価。

article.articleHeadline: Botulism Toxin in Vietnam: Health authorities respond to food safety concerns
article.articleSummary: As of March 21, 2026, Da Nang has reported two new suspected cases of food poisoning linked to fermented fish, specifically Ca u chua, a local delicacy. The patients were hospitalized and are receiving care at Phuoc Son Regional Medical Center. In response, health authorities are mobilizing intensive-care resources and coordinating with higher-level facilities to manage the situation effectively. The Vietnam Food Safety Authority has initiated a trace of ingredients and is testing food and patient samples, with strict penalties for any violations. Public awareness campaigns are underway to educate the community about the dangers of consuming handmade fermented fish that do not meet hygiene standards. Earlier this month, three children were hospitalized due to botulinum poisoning from similar sources, prompting the World Health Organization to supply Botulism Antitoxin Heptavalent vials, which are not stored domestically in Vietnam. This follows previous assistance from WHO in 2020 and 2023.

triage.triage_reason: ボツリヌス中毒による複数の食中毒事例、入院患者あり、公衆衛生への深刻な影響、WHOの緊急支援が必要な状況であり、IHR基準2つ以上該当。食品安全に関する異常事象として重要。
triage.notes: ボツリヌス毒素による食中毒が2026年3月時点で複数例報告。同月初旬に3児がボツリヌス中毒で入院し、WHO から抗毒素供給を受けている。発酵魚製品（Ca u chua）が感染源と特定。ベトナムでは抗毒素の国内備蓄がなく、国際支援が必須。公衆衛生上の重大な関心事項。

article.articleHeadline: Influenza in Thailand: Current trends and public health recommendations
article.articleSummary: Influenza activity in Thailand has increased significantly in 2026, with 137,276 cumulative cases reported from January 1 to March 9, resulting in 8 deaths. The Ministry of Public Health's Department of Disease Control highlights that the virus spreads primarily through respiratory droplets and contact with infected surfaces. The most affected demographic is children aged 0–14, although a decline in weekly cases has been noted, the overall numbers remain above the five-year average. A resurgence is expected mid-year due to seasonal patterns. Most fatalities have occurred among the elderly and individuals with pre-existing health conditions who were not vaccinated. Public health officials are urging the public to maintain hygiene practices, such as regular handwashing, wearing masks when symptomatic, and avoiding crowded areas to mitigate the spread of the virus.

triage.headline_ja: タイのインフルエンザ：現在の傾向と公衆衛生上の勧告
triage.triage_reason: タイでのインフルエンザ活動は5年平均を上回るレベルで増加しており、137,276症例と8死亡が報告されている。ただし、週間症例数の減少傾向が見られ、国際的拡大の明示的な証拠は記事に記載されていない。情報不足のため経過観察が必要。
triage.notes: IHR基準は2つ該当し、WPROスクリーニング基準は4つ該当している。ただし、記事は季節的インフルエンザの通常の監視レポートの性質が強く、社会的・政治的関心の詳細情報が限定的であるため、WATCH判定とした。週間症例数の減少トレンドは肯定的な兆候であるが、年半の再流行予測があり、引き続き注視が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Enterovirus 71 in Vietnam: Seasonal peak leads to increased pediatric cases
article.articleSummary: In Ho Chi Minh City, hand, foot, and mouth disease (HFMD) cases have reached 837 in the latest week, marking a 97.1% increase from the average. This year, the city has reported a total of 7,294 cases, with the highest rates observed in wards Long Huong, Long Dien, and Thuong Tan, exceeding 100 cases per 100,000 residents. Pediatric hospitals are experiencing a surge in HFMD visits, with Children's Hospital 1 treating 36 children, 46% of whom are severe cases. Despite the increase in cases, current treatment numbers are lower than the same period last year. The Ho Chi Minh City Department of Health (HCDC) has issued warnings about the rapid spread and potential outbreaks, particularly in nurseries and schools. Nationwide, Vietnam has recorded over 107,000 HFMD cases in 2025, a 29% increase from 2024. HFMD, primarily caused by enteroviruses, predominantly affects children under five and spreads through the digestive tract or contact with contaminated surfaces. Prevention strategies focus on hygiene and early detection.

triage.headline_ja: ベトナムのエンテロウイルス71：季節性ピークにより小児症例が増加
triage.triage_reason: ベトナムにおいて手足口病（HFMD）の症例が異常な増加を示し、IHR基準2項目（深刻な公衆衛生への影響、異常/予想外性）に該当する。小児を含む多数の患者、重症症例の存在、国内外での急速な拡大が認められ、WPROスクリーニング基準でも複数項目に該当。フルRRAの実施が必要。
triage.notes: 2026年3月時点での報告。ホーチミン市で最新週837例（前年同期比97.1%増）、通年で7,294例。2025年全国では107,000例超（2024年比29%増）と記載。小児病院での46%が重症例。主要な公衆衛生上の懸念として保育園・学校での集団発生リスクが指摘されている。Enterovirus 71は手足口病の主要病原体。

article.articleHeadline: Scabies in India: Contaminated water linked to skin disease outbreak
article.articleSummary: In Danvakheda village, Betul district, Madhya Pradesh, an outbreak of skin diseases, primarily scabies, has affected at least 20 children as of March 21, 2026. Symptoms include severe itching, cold, cough, and fever. The outbreak was first reported on March 15, prompting the organization of a medical camp and the dispatch of a medical team to address the situation. Digvijaya Singh has attributed the outbreak to contaminated drinking water, calling for urgent government action to ensure safe water supplies and investigate contamination sources. He highlighted a previous fatal outbreak in the same area six months prior, emphasizing the need for improved medical facilities and accountability among officials. While the Chief Medical Health Officer, Dr. Manoj Hurmade, confirmed the response efforts, there are no details regarding laboratory-confirmed diagnoses in the report.

article.articleHeadline: Rabies in Thailand: Outbreak zone established to control transmission
article.articleSummary: Yasothon Province in Thailand has declared a 5-km rabies outbreak zone in Pa Tio District following the confirmation of rabies in a dog from Pho Sai Subdistrict. The dog bite incident occurred on March 18, and subsequent testing at the Lower Northeastern Veterinary Research Center confirmed the presence of the virus. In response, public health measures were implemented, including the vaccination of a child who was bitten, who is currently stable at home. Six additional high-risk contacts have been identified and have completed their vaccinations. The outbreak zone encompasses 18 villages, affecting approximately 3,100 dogs and cats. To date, over 300 dogs have been vaccinated, achieving an 85% coverage rate, with full vaccination of households expected within 1-2 days. Authorities are urging adherence to the 5Y guidelines and prompt medical attention for any animal bites to mitigate further transmission of rabies.

triage.headline_ja: タイの狂犬病：感染予防のためのアウトブレイクゾーン確立
triage.triage_reason: タイで狂犬病の確認とアウトブレイク対応が進行中だが、人への感染は限定的で管理下にある。スクリーニング基準では異常性と流行可能性が該当するが、情報不足と対応体制の充実により、現時点ではWATCH段階での経過観察が適切。
triage.notes: 記事はタイのヤソートン県で犬から確認された狂犬病に関するもので、噛まれた子ども1人と高リスク接触者6人が予防接種を完了している。当局による積極的な対応（5km隔離ゾーン、ワクチン接種キャンペーン）が進行中。人への重症例は報告されていないが、犬・猫約3,100頭が曝露され、人獣共通感染症としての潜在的リスクが存在。続報監視が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Varicella in Vietnam: Newborns face severe complications from infection
article.articleSummary: On March 21, 2026, a 12-day-old newborn in Vietnam was hospitalized with varicella, complicated by pneumonia and severe respiratory failure. The infant presented with fever and a generalized vesicular rash, leading to rapid deterioration requiring mechanical ventilation and intensive care. After 10 days of treatment, including antiviral therapy and antibiotics, the baby's condition improved significantly, with resolution of skin lesions and stabilization of health. Varicella-Zoster virus transmission occurs through respiratory droplets and direct contact, posing serious risks to newborns, including pneumonia and potential death. Health experts recommend that pregnant women minimize exposure to suspected cases and consider vaccination, while families with newborns should monitor for symptoms and seek prompt medical attention. Preventive strategies emphasize hygiene, handwashing, and isolation to protect vulnerable individuals.

triage.notes: 単一の新生児重篤症例の報告であり、流行や集団発生の兆候は記事に記載されていない。水痘は既知の法定感染症であり、ベトナムでの認識・対応体制が存在すると考えられる。症例が重篤であることは確認されるが、複数症例や地域的拡大の証拠がないため、現段階ではWATCH（要経過観察）と判定。続報で集団発生や異常な流行パターンが報告された場合はPICKUPに昇格させる。

article.articleHeadline: Mpox Clade II in India: New variant prompts global health concerns and monitoring
article.articleSummary: A new recombinant variant of mpox, resulting from the combination of clades Ib and IIb, has emerged, raising alarms at the World Health Organization. The first case in India was reported in 2025, followed by a second case in the United Kingdom, although no chain transmission has been detected. This variant poses challenges for detection and control, highlighting potential gaps in diagnostics and treatment. A recent study published in the New England Journal of Medicine indicated that tecovirimat, the primary antiviral treatment, does not significantly reduce recovery time in immunocompetent patients, necessitating a reassessment of current therapeutic approaches. The WHO has called for enhanced global surveillance and ongoing research to address the evolving nature of the virus, emphasizing the need for cautious monitoring and updated treatment strategies, as of March 21, 2026.

triage.notes: 新型組み換えMpox変異株（Clade Ib/IIbの組み合わせ）の出現。インドでの初症例は2025年、英国での第2症例報告。現在の標準治療（テコビリマット）の効果が限定的であることが判明し、治療戦略の見直しが必要。WHOが強化された全球的監視を呼び掛けており、国際的な関心・支援必要性が高い。

article.articleHeadline: Dengue in Vietnam: Challenges in managing severe cases and prevention efforts
article.articleSummary: Dengue fever poses a significant public health challenge in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam, with an increasing number of adults affected. Recent statistics indicate that severe cases have escalated from approximately 15% to between 17% and 19% in recent years. The disease is prevalent year-round, with peak transmission occurring from June to October, largely influenced by urbanization and climate change, as Aedes mosquitoes thrive in clean-water containers found in homes. Many patients resort to at-home treatments, leading to delayed care and worsening health outcomes. Families face economic and social disruptions due to the disease's impact. Key prevention strategies include eliminating mosquito breeding sites, covering water storage, utilizing nets, and implementing vector-control measures. Urgent care is critical for patients exhibiting warning signs such as high fever, severe abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, and bleeding, as these can indicate progression to dengue shock syndrome or other severe complications.

article.articleHeadline: Human Infection with Avian Influenza in India: Culling measures implemented to control outbreak
article.articleSummary: As of March 21, 2026, avian influenza has been confirmed in Kozhikode district, Kerala, prompting authorities to cull approximately 15,000 birds across five panchayats: Panangad, Olavanna, Kakodi, Perumanna, and Nallalam. This action aims to contain the outbreak by eliminating both wild and domestic poultry within a one-kilometer radius of the infected zones. While specific details regarding laboratory confirmations or the source of infection remain undisclosed, the focus is on rapidly reducing potential reservoirs of the virus to safeguard local farms and communities from further transmission.

article.articleHeadline: Tuberculosis in Brazil: Early diagnosis crucial to combat ongoing health challenge
article.articleSummary: In 2024, Brazil reported 85,936 new tuberculosis (TB) cases and 6,315 deaths, highlighting the urgent need for effective public health strategies. Goiás state alone recorded 5,498 confirmed cases from 2021 to 2025, with increasing mortality rates. Ceap-Sol emphasizes the importance of early diagnosis and adherence to treatment to mitigate this persistent health issue. Symptoms such as a prolonged cough, fever, loss of appetite, and weight loss should prompt immediate medical investigation. TB is primarily transmitted through the air, particularly before treatment begins, making timely diagnosis critical. Laboratory tests and imaging are essential for accurate diagnosis, while treatment, which lasts a minimum of six months, is highly effective if completed. Interruptions in treatment can lead to drug resistance, complicating efforts to control the disease. Vulnerable populations, including children, are prioritized for BCG vaccination, and services are provided free of charge through the Unified Health System (SUS). Early detection is vital to reduce complications and prevent further transmission.
